text:
maria: Pushed a small PR to normalize code example identifiers per-language and add a docs-snippet linter. It updates quickstarts, SDK snippets, and the migration guide. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/4928

alex: Nice. What's the linter doing exactly?

maria: It checks three things: 1) language fence label (python/js/ts), 2) identifier casing matches language convention (snake_case for python, camelCase for js/ts), 3) no cross-language canonicalization of variable names. I added the linter to docs CI as an optional job for now.

jamal: Optional job is fine to start. Do you have examples of failures?

maria: Yep, included in the PR description. Example failure from a migrated snippet:

```
// js
const resp = await client.generate({ model_name: "redwood-alpha", prompt: "hi" })
```

The linter flags `model_name` in the js block and suggests `modelName`.

tara: Love that. Can the linter also suggest idiomatic replacements rather than just flagging? That'll speed up reviews.

maria: It currently suggests replacements using a small ruleset: snake_case <-> camelCase mappings for common identifiers (model_name <-> modelName, api_key <-> apiKey, dataset_id <-> datasetId). We can expand.

alex: Any impact on existing docs anchors/links? We had a few anchors that changed variable names inside headings.

maria: Ran the link-checker too. Fixed 4 internal anchor mismatches. One external link to security policy is blocked pending product signoff; left a TODO in the PR.

jamal: Good catch. Also, we should avoid changing identifiers inside code blocks that are API contract examples (like request/response JSON) if the backend actually expects camelCase. How are we detecting that?

maria: The linter rules include an allowlist comment marker. If an example is intentionally canonicalized to API payload naming (e.g., // api-payload) reviewers can add `<!-- docs-lint: allow-case -->` above the block. The CI will skip flagged blocks with that marker.

tara: Solid. On the glossary front, did you change anything? There's the ongoing serving/inference alias debate.

maria: Tagged lexicon-bot to create a suggestion to map search terms to both.

lexicon-bot: Created glossary suggestion #239: "serving (alias) -> inference" and added search synonyms so both terms surface.

alex: Can we add a short CONTRIBUTING blurb? One paragraph that says: "Prefer idiomatic identifiers per language in code examples; if the example demonstrates an API payload use the api-payload marker."

tara: I'll draft the paragraph after the PR merges and add it to docs/contributing.md.

maria: One more thing — I added a small test matrix in the PR showing sample snippets across Python/JS/TS and how they should look. After merge I'll open a follow-up to apply the script across other repos (examples repo, tutorials).

jamal: Reviewing now. Left three inline comments: two wording tweaks and one around the allowlist marker syntax.

ci-bot: docs-snippet-lint job started for PR #4928. Report will post as a comment when complete.

maria: Thanks all. Please review; if +1s by EOD I'll flip the linter to required in CI and run the bulk migration in a separate PR.
